statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The rates-driven risk-off session closed with an observed retracement, and index futures are now inside the maintenance halt with no live price path.
recommendation: Tail stays below the block threshold, so the mapped state remains WATCH. The narrow flagged window covers the 24 September U.S. cash open, where an aligned rates, energy and semiconductor backdrop could produce opening continuation.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes off its low after a 2007-high 10-year yield; futures enter the maintenance halt
body: The 23 September U.S. session ended risk-off but orderly. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,470.29, down 262.10 points or 0.85%, inside a 30,353.88 to 30,706.23 range and about 116 points above the low, so the index did not settle on its lows. Nasdaq-100 futures last printed 30,773.00, down 0.82%, roughly 130 points above their 30,643.25 low, before the 21:00 UTC CME maintenance halt. That halt is why this hour carries no live NQ price path. Rates drove the session: the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 15 basis points to 5.11% after an intraday peak near 5.135%, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year added roughly 13 basis points to about 4.90%. S&P Global's flash composite PMI reached 58.4, a 62-month high, with services at 58.7 and input costs the steepest since October 2022. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said further policy adjustments are likely to be needed, and October FOMC hike pricing moved to roughly 71%. Energy added to the inflation channel, with WTI up about 2.4% to roughly $92.71 while Brent held just below $100 as a partial restoration of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline offset some Strait of Hormuz supply concern. Latest-session shared context showed all seven tracked semiconductors lower and five of eight megacaps down, though Microsoft, Meta and Tesla closed higher, so megacap participation was dispersed rather than uniformly one-way. Against that, the VIX at 15.18 remains low in absolute terms and the close-off-lows retracement shows mean reversion still functioning. That combination supports elevated Stress with Tail held in the watch band. The published conditional peak is the 24 September cash open at 13:30 UTC, where opening continuation from an already aligned backdrop is the specific structure that would deny retracement, with the Chinese state visit to Washington adding a headline channel into semiconductor and AI names.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours divide cleanly at the 23 September U.S. data window. Through the overnight and European morning, Claude published Tail between 10 and 16 with Stress in the mid-30s as the Nasdaq-100 held a quiet uptrend and then a neutral range. The 14:00 UTC hour marked the regime change: the flash PMI beat, its steepest input-price reading since October 2022 and the accompanying yield surge pushed Tail to 25 and Stress to 54 in a trend-down assessment. Tail then settled back to 22-24 with Stress between 53 and 57 for the rest of the cash session, because the decline stayed orderly and retracements remained available rather than becoming one-way extension.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are shaped by an unresolved rates and energy backdrop rather than by an observed one-way equity path. The current hour is the CME maintenance halt, so no live NQ structure prints until the 22:00 UTC Globex restart. Overnight risk then stays in the low-to-watch band through the Asian session, with the Tokyo open and the 07:00 UTC European cash and bond opens as the first cross-asset confirmation checkpoints. Risk builds conditionally into the 24 September U.S. sequence: jobless claims at 12:30 UTC raise whipsaw rather than sustained Tail, and the published peak sits at the 13:30 UTC cash open, where opening continuation from an aligned backdrop would be the structure that denies retracement. New Home Sales at 14:00 UTC keeps risk just below the block band before it decays through the U.S. midday and ticks up modestly into the power hour. The Chinese state visit to Washington is a live headline channel into semiconductor and AI names across the European and U.S. hours. Every forecast hour beyond the current one describes a conditional path, not observed structure.
